hints: Notice the phrase rebounds along its original path with $14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in and $7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ out, so velocity changes sign.
Recall impulse $F\Delta t = \Delta p = m(v-u)$ and convert the $200 \text{ g}$ mass to $0.200 \text{ kg}$ before multiplying.
Add the two speeds to get the magnitude of velocity change over the $0.60 \text{ s}$ contact, then divide $m$ times that change by time.
walkthrough: Convert mass to SI units: $m = 200 \text{ g} = 0.200 \text{ kg}$, with contact time $\Delta t = 0.60 \text{ s}$.
Choose a direction as positive, for example towards the cushion. Then initial velocity $u = +14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and rebound velocity $v = -7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Find the change in velocity: $\Delta v = v - u = -7.0 - 14.0 = -21.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the magnitude is $21.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Find the magnitude of momentum change: $|\Delta p| = m|\Delta v| = 0.200 \times 21.0 = 4.2 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Use average force from impulse: $F = |\Delta p| / \Delta t = 4.2 / 0.60 = 7.0 \text{ N}$. This is option D.

options.A: Gives $1.4 \text{ N}$, which is $m \times 7.0$ without dividing by $0.60 \text{ s}$ and ignores the $14.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ incoming speed.
options.B: Gives about $2.3 \text{ N}$ from $(14.0-7.0)=7.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, treating rebound as a slowing down rather than a reversal of direction.
options.C: Gives $4.2 \text{ N}$, which is the magnitude of momentum change $0.20 \times 21.0$ but omits division by the contact time $0.60 \text{ s}$.
options.D: Gives $7.0 \text{ N}$ from total velocity change $14.0+7.0$ divided by $0.60 \text{ s}$ with $0.200 \text{ kg}$ mass.
